name: Slow Cooker BBQ Country Style Pork Ribs over Rice
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified at 576 cal / 44g protein per serving over 4 servings for the meat alone; over rice it is a 640 cal dinner with a very strong protein ratio. Five-minute prep slow cooker dish. The live Brazilian-Style Pork Ribs Bowls are a different cut and flavor profile, but flag for the dedup stage since both are rib-and-rice bowls. | HARVEST: Source recipe is ribs only; rice is not part of the source ingredient list.
intro_html: Five minutes of work in the morning, barbecue for a week. Country style ribs are cut from the shoulder, which means they are cheap, forgiving, and they turn to shreds after a long slow cook. Pile them over rice and you have 43 grams of protein sitting at about $2.30 a bowl.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: BBQ Sauce, 3.5 cups: ~$4.36. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 18oz bottles.
Pantry seasonings (garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, salt, black pepper): ~$0.37. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $32.21 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.30 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $34.96 across 14 servings, roughly $2.50 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $12.90 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $47.86. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.30 a bowl for slow cooked barbecue pork over rice. A barbecue joint plate would cost you several times that and would not be waiting in your fridge on Wednesday.
shop_smart: Buy the whole pork shoulder, not the trimmed ribs. Country style ribs come off the shoulder anyway. Buying the bigger primal cut usually drops the per pound price, and you cut it down at home.
Barbecue sauce is the second biggest line. Buy the large bottle of store brand rather than a boutique one. This batch uses a lot of it, and the big bottle is often half the price per ounce.
The dry rub is entirely jars you own. Garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, salt and pepper. That is the whole seasoning bill and it costs pennies per batch.
Rice is the cheapest filler on the board. Buy the big bag. It stretches this batch and about thirty more after it.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into thick rib style strips and pat them dry so the rub sticks.
Stir the garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, salt and black pepper together and rub it over every surface of the pork.
Slice the yellow onions and spread them across the bottom of the slow cooker to make a bed the meat can sit on.
Lay the pork on the onions, sprinkle the brown sugar over the top, and pour about half the barbecue sauce across everything.
Cover and cook on low until the meat pulls apart with light pressure from a fork.
Cook the rice near the end so it is fresh and hot when the pork is done.
Shred the pork right in the cooker, stir in the rest of the barbecue sauce and the juices, then combine with the rice in your big pot.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container so nobody gets shorted on meat. Every bowl lands near 605 calories and 43 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from themagicalslowcooker.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.

head.description: Slow cooker barbecue country style pork ribs shredded over rice, built for 14 servings. 605 calories, 43g protein, about $2.30 per serving.
head.keywords: slow cooker country style ribs, bbq pork rice bowls, crockpot pork ribs, budget bbq meal prep, cheap pork dinner
steps: Cut the pork shoulder into rib style strips and coat with a rub of garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, salt and pepper.
Layer sliced onions in the slow cooker, add the pork, sprinkle with brown sugar and pour over half the barbecue sauce.
Cook on low until the pork shreds easily with a fork.
Cook the rice separately near the end.
Shred the pork, stir in the remaining sauce and juices, and serve over the rice.
